symptoms: The job reads some tables and fails on another, with an authorization error naming the credential-vending API
The failure is on the data path and not on the catalog metadata call: the table was described, and then the read or the write stopped
Granting more Lake Formation permission on the table does not change the outcome
likely_causes: The job runtime role lacks the lakeformation:GetDataAccess IAM permission, which is what lets Lake Formation vend the temporary credential
The caller has no SELECT or SUPER permission on the table the credential is being requested for
Credential vending for full table access is not enabled in the data lake settings
The table location is not registered with Lake Formation, so there is no stored credential to vend
diagnostic_steps: Read the access model the job declares: the credential-vending path is the one Lake Formation uses, and a job that declares no access model is not on it
Read the IAM policy of the job runtime role for lakeformation:GetDataAccess, which the AWS policy example grants for both fine-grained access control and Full Table Access
Read the Lake Formation grants on the table for the runtime role, separating DESCRIBE from SELECT: describing a table is not reading it
Read whether the table location is registered with Lake Formation, because an unregistered location has no stored credential to vend
fixes: Grant lakeformation:GetDataAccess to the job runtime role in IAM, scoped as narrowly as the account allows
Grant the Lake Formation permission the operation needs on the table: SELECT to read, and ALL to write or delete under Full Table Access
Register the table location with Lake Formation when the intent is that Lake Formation vends the credential
unsafe_fixes: Granting Super on the catalog to IAMAllowedPrincipals, which removes the governance the job was placed under

Widening the S3 policy of the runtime role to bypass the credential path: for a registered location the data access path goes through the Lake Formation stored credentials regardless of the IAM permission of the runtime role, so the wider policy does not take effect and the governance is weakened for nothing
verification: Re-run the job and confirm the same table is read; then confirm with a principal that does NOT hold the grant that the read still fails, because a fix that works for everyone removed the control instead of correcting it
rollback: Revoke the IAM permission and the Lake Formation grant that were added. If the location was registered, unregistering it changes the access path for every consumer of that location and is not a rollback of this job alone
